Hi Samantha — great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and a couple of follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity for FastFin properly. I'm attaching a short worksheet (fastfin_capacity_estimate.xlsx) you can fill; I also pasted the key questions below.

What we heard on the call (high level):
- Primary use: real-time assistant inside the product for customer support + automated financial summaries.
- Latency SLO: 200ms p99 for short queries, 95th percentile for summary jobs okay up to ~1s.
- Security: likely needs dedicated environment; SOC2 evidence requested.

Key sizing & deployment questions (please confirm):
1) Target sustained TPS (inference requests per second) and expected peak TPS (including bursts).
2) Typical concurrency per session and total concurrent sessions.
3) Token mix: average prompt tokens and average response tokens, plus percent of long-sequence jobs (>2k tokens).
4) Preferred model family (we discussed open Llama variants, Mistral, or customer-provided model). Any preference for quantized variants?
5) Deployment mode: Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) vs Private VPC/on-prem — what's FastFin leaning toward?
6) Compliance & networking constraints: egress restrictions, IP allow lists, KMS requirement.

Next steps I propose: you fill the attached worksheet and we schedule a 30–45m sizing call with our infra architect (Marissa) to walk through the numbers and pick GPU type (A100 vs H100), concurrency strategy, and burst plan. After that we'll produce a committed capacity recommendation and a first-pass pricing outline.

Thanks — I can be flexible on timing; are you available Thu or Fri morning PST?

Best,
Rafael

1) For the 5% long-sequence summaries (~4k tokens output) — are those batch jobs (asynchronous) or do they need to meet the same p99 latency SLO?
2) Do you expect model switching per request (e.g., some endpoints using fine-tuned variant, others using base open model)? If so, what percent of traffic will hit the fine-tuned model?
3) Any hard requirement for on-prem hardware (air-gapped)? You mentioned Private is an option if procurement requires it — helpful to know if that's a must-have or a ‘nice-to-have’.

Quick note on GPUs: for the numbers you gave, our typical starting recommendation is 2–4 H100s (or equivalently higher-count A100 80GBs) for the Dedicated pool if you want headroom for the burst profile and the long-sequence jobs. H100s give better throughput for large context lengths and mixed-precision, but we can build a cost-effective A100 plan if H100 availability is limited. Marissa will bring examples of throughput (TPS) vs GPUs for the specific model family you're evaluating.

Action items for Thu call:

- Confirm burst handling (queueing vs autoscale vs routing to hosted).
- Procurement timeline and contract ask (Tom).

See you Thu 10am PST.

Rafael

Thanks — looping in Aditya (infra perf) for the sizing call as well. Quick tech notes ahead of our Thu meeting so we can make the call concrete:

- Burst handling: For short spikes up to ~4x sustained TPS (your 180 TPS peak vs 45 sustained), we typically recommend a two-layer strategy:
  * Reserved Dedicated pool sized to cover sustained TPS + baseline concurrency.
  * Autoscale/burst to Hosted or additional reserved nodes for short events to avoid overcommitting monthly reserved capacity.

- GPU guidance: For 7B–13B models with your token mix, approximate ballpark throughput per GPU (single-model, fp16):
  * H100 80GB: ~750–1,200 short-query TPS (1–2 token responses) with batching efficiency; better for long-sequence 4K outputs.
  * A100 80GB: ~400–800 short-query TPS; reduced throughput for >2k contexts.

Given your concurrency (~750 sessions) and burst profile, a starting Dedicated config could be:
Option A (cost-efficiency, A100s): 6 x A100-80GB reserved (handles sustained and modest bursts with autoscale to hosted)
Option B (performance + long-context, H100s): 2 x H100-80GB reserved + autoscale buffer for bursts (preferred if long-sequence jobs must be low-latency)

- Token mix & caching: If many requests share prefixes (customer metadata, static prompts), enabling prefix/KV caching can reduce token compute by 20–40% for short Q/A. Please flag if you have identical templates across requests.

- Model switching: If you plan to route a minority (e.g., 10–20%) of requests to the fine-tuned model, we recommend colocating a hot pool for the fine-tuned model to avoid cold-model load penalties.

I've attached a capacity calc (dedicated_capacity_calc_v2.xlsx) with throughput rows you can edit. We'll walk through the tradeoffs and expected monthly committed GPU counts on Thu.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Infra Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
